subject: Media Literacy
title: Smartphones: Media in Every Pocket
description: A 60-second lesson on Smartphones: Media in Every Pocket.

hook.text: The average person checks their smartphone 96 times a day. That's once every 10 waking minutes.

buildup.text: Smartphones combined the newspaper, radio, TV, camera, and library into one pocket device.

discovery.text: More people now access news through smartphones than through any other medium in history.

twist.text: Constant access means constant exposure. Media isn't something you consume — it's an environment you live in.

climax.text: The smartphone didn't just change media. It made media inescapable.

punchline.text: You don't use your phone. You live inside it.

quiz.question: How has the smartphone changed media consumption?
options: Media became a constant environment, not an occasional activity
